sentences.text: Revenue Divisional Officer / Land ... vs Mahesh Kumar Jaju And
10 Ors on 7 November, 2024

Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty
 L.A.A.S.No.343 Of 2015
Judgment:

(Per the Hon'ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili) Heard Smt. Babita, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Appeals, appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer and Sri V.
Ravi Kiran Rao, learned Senior Counsel for respondents.

2. This Appeal, under Section 54 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short, 'the Act') is filed by the Land Acquisition Officer challenging the order, dated 30.03.2011 passed in O.P.147 of 1996 on the file of the I Additional District Judge, Nizamabad (hereinafter referred to as "the Reference Court").
3.

The brief facts of the case are that on a requisition made by the Executive Engineer (R &B),
Nizamabad, an extent of land admeasuring 1,213.52 sq. meters, along with building situated at Nizamabad town, belonging to the respondents/claimants, was acquired for the purpose of constructing Railway over- ::2:: AKS,J & LNA,J bridge; that draft notification under Section 4 (1) of the Act and declaration under Section 6 of the Act were published in the A.P. Gazette on 13.11.1994 and 15.11.1994 respectively; that the Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting necessary enquiry passed an award,
dated 25.09.1995, granting compensation of @ Rs.1100/- per sq. yd. for H.Nos.7-1-50, 7-1-58/2,
7-1-58/4 and 7-1-58/5 and @ Rs.940/- per sq. yd. for the remaining land.
4. Not being satisfied with the Award, the respondents/claimants sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was numbered as O.P.No.147 of 1996 on the file of the Reference Court.
5. Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/claimants, RW.1 was examined and Exs.B1 to B3 were marked.
On behalf of the Land Acquisition Officer, PWs.1 to 5 were examined and Exs.A1 to A42 were marked.

6. The Reference Court, on appreciation of the entire evidence and material available on record,
passed the ::3:: AKS,J & LNA,J impugned order enhancing the market value of the total acquired lands to Rs. @ Rs.1,700/- per sq. yd., apart from granting statutory benefits under the Act to the Revenue Divisional Officer / Land ... vs Mahesh Kumar Jaju And 10 Ors on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79058263/
1 respondents/claimants.
7.
Aggrieved by the impugned order, dated 30.03.2011 passed by the Reference Court, the present appeal is filed.
8. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-LAO had contended that the Reference Court has erroneously enhanced the market value without there being any material.

Learned counsel further contended that the Reference Court improperly relied upon Exs.A5 and A6, which do not show that these Exhibits are similar in nature or nearer to the acquired land, as they are situated in a different locality.
Learned Assistant Government Pleader further contended that enhancing of compensation by 50% is unsustainable.

9. Per contra, learned Senior Counsel for the respondents/claimants had contended that the ::4::
AKS,J & LNA,J Reference Court has rightly enhanced the compensation after due consideration of the evidence and material placed on record, including examination of five witnesses and documents supporting the claim.
Learned counsel further contended that Exs.A5 and A6 were rightly relied upon by the Reference Court, which and also recorded detailed reasons.
Therefore, there are no merits in the Appeal and the same is liable to be dismissed.
10. A perusal of the record discloses that the lands acquired for the Railway over-Bridge are situated in the middle of the city.

The two documents i.e., Exs.A5 and A6 relied upon by the Reference Court are prior to the date of notification and evidence placed on record also shows that they are nearer to the acquired lands and are similar in nature.
The Reference Court has also observed that the respondents/claimants supported their claim by way of sketch of the area documents and other relevant documents.
::5:: AKS,J & LNA,J 11.
In the light of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Reference Court was justified in enhancing the market value of the total acquired lands to Rs.1,700/- per sq.yd.
Therefore, this Court does not find any illegality or irregularity in the impugned order passed by the Reference Court.
12. The Appeal is accordingly, dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.

_________________________________ ABHINAND KUMAR SHAVILI, J ___________________________________ LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY, J Date:
07.11.2024.
